description: Linopy is a Python optimisation-modelling package published by the PyPSA community. It connects labelled multidimensional data in xarray and Pandas to mathematical-programming solvers. Users define continuous or integer variables, coordinate-indexed constraints and objectives, then export or solve linear, mixed-integer and quadratic problems. NetCDF input/output preserves the labelled model representation, and optional Dask operations support larger arrays. Geographic extent, spatial detail and time resolution are determined by the user's coordinates and data, not a fixed energy-system dataset. Source, examples and package installation instructions are public and free under MIT. A limitation is that a suitable solver must be available separately; commercial solver licences remain distinct from the open modelling package. Linopy supplies optimisation building blocks, not calibrated infrastructure equations or guarantees of solver feasibility. It is relevant to capacity-planning and dispatch model development in the same project community as PyPSA (model-pypsa). The README's comparative performance chart was not reproduced in this review, and no optimisation problem was executed.
